name: openssl
description: The OpenSSL toolkit: TLS certificate inspection, generation, encryption, and protocol testing from the command line.

flags.description: Open a raw TLS connection to inspect a server certificate.
Decode and display a certificate file.
Encrypt a file with a password.

examples.output:
Connection state... : OK
Protocol version... : TLSv1.3
Verification...    : OK
examples.explanation: Connects to the server over TLS and reports the negotiated protocol and certificate verification — the definitive "is TLS working?" test.
Shows who a certificate belongs to and when it expires — the check for "why did TLS suddenly break?".

examples.command: echo | openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
examples.explanation: One-liner: remote certificate expiry dates without any files — perfect for expiry monitoring scripts.
Computes a checksum to compare against the publisher's published hash.

about: openssl is both a library and a CLI. The s_client subcommand is the universal TLS debugger when curl is too abstract; x509 decodes certificates; req generates certificate signing requests (CSRs) for real certificates. Note LibreSSL (macOS/BSD) differs subtly in available subcommands.
useCases: Generate hashes and self-signed dev certificates.
mistakes: Confusing the private key file (.key, never share) with the certificate (.crt/.pem, public).
warnings: Private keys generated with openssl must be protected like passwords (chmod 600, never committed).
